title: Delta–Y Conversion: A Triangle Becomes a Star
topic: Delta (Δ) to Y (T) conversion — three resistors arranged as a triangle between nodes A, B, C are equivalent to three resistors meeting at a central node N. The Y resistor opposite each Δ branch carries the product of its two adjacent Δ resistors over the sum of all three. Used to unsnarl bridge circuits that have no series/parallel reduction.

beats.narration: When a circuit has no series or parallel pairs to collapse, sometimes you can convert a triangle of resistors into a star — same terminals, simpler shape.

elements.content: Stuck on a circuit? Turn the triangle into a star.

beats.narration: Three nodes A, B, C with a resistor between every pair — that's a delta. Each branch carries the two-node label R sub A B, R sub B C, R sub C A.

elements.content: Node A top, node B bottom-right, node C bottom-left
Resistor R_AB between A and B (right side of triangle)
Resistor R_BC between B and C (bottom of triangle)
Resistor R_CA between C and A (left side of triangle)
Node labels A, B, C and resistor labels R_AB, R_BC, R_CA

beats.narration: Hold the three corner terminals fixed. Slide the three resistors inward — now they meet at a single point N. Same three nodes, same external behaviour, but Y-shaped.

elements.content: Three resistors morph from triangle sides to spokes meeting at centre N
Centre node N appears once morph completes

beats.narration: Each Y spoke equals the product of its two adjacent delta sides divided by the sum of all three. R sub A is the product of the two branches meeting at A — divided by the total.

elements.content: spoke = product of adjacent branches over total

beats.narration: Now any bridge or mesh that defeated series-parallel reduction is back in play. Convert the awkward triangle and the rest collapses.

elements.content: Triangle → Star. Same terminals, simpler topology.
the rescue trick for any bridge circuit
